title: B2-19 · Vocabulary of media and communication

blocks.text: B2-19 · Vocabulary of media and communication

From B2-01 read articles, press releases and interviews: it is time to give a precise name to the world that produces them. A editorial staff has its roles (the editor, the editor, the correspondent, who checks the facts) and its genres (the inquiry, the editorial, the column, the scoop); traditional printing changes (downloads, digital subscriptions, layoffs, newsletters); social platforms have a new vocabulary, which Arabic has created in a few years ( ⁧تغريدة⁩ , ⁧وسم⁩ , ⁧مؤثر⁩ , ⁧خوارزمية⁩ ); institutional communication has its tools (the spokesperson, the campaigns, public relations). In this unit you learn this vocabulary by field , the most frequent placements ( ⁧اِنْتَشَرَ عَلَى نِطَاقٍ وَاسِعٍ⁩ , ⁧الأَكْثَرُ تَدَاوُلًا⁩ ) and the way in which Arabic forms neologisms (limestone, adaptation, new word from an ancient root). Three weeks, in parallel with MAG-01.

rows: B2 · Module B2.4 Variation and production
B2-01 (read an article), B2-07 and B2-08 (interviews, attribution), INT-05 (disinformation)
16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 230–232), plus the MAG track in separate blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, websites of Arab newspapers and televisions (Appendix C), sessions with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. appoint the roles of a editorial staff and major journalistic genres;
2. understand and use the vocabulary of the crisis and the transformation of the press (copies, subscriptions, dismissals, Newsletter);
3. understand and use the vocabulary of social platforms (post, tweet, follower, hashtag, algorithm, content Sponsored);
4. understand the vocabulary of institutional communication (spokesman, campaign, public relations, survey);
5. recognize how Arab neologisms of the media form.

⁧لَيْلَى: مُحَرِّرُونَ. يَسْتَقْبِلُونَ الأَخْبَارَ مِنَ الوَكَالَاتِ وَمِنْ مُرَاسِلِينَا فِي المَنَاطِقِ، وَيُعِيدُونَ صِيَاغَتَهَا. وَفِي الزَّاوِيَةِ قِسْمُ التَّحَقُّقِ: ثَلَاثَةُ زُمَلَاءَ يَتَحَقَّقُونَ مِنَ الصُّوَرِ وَالفِيدْيُوهَاتِ قَبْلَ النَّشْرِ.⁩

Laylā: Editors. They get news from agencies and correspondents in the regions, and they rewrite it. And in the corner there is the verification service: three colleagues check photos and videos before publication.
⁧لَيْلَى: أَنَا أَكْتُبُ التَّحْقِيقَاتِ: مَوَاضِيعُ طَوِيلَةٌ تَحْتَاجُ إِلَى أَسَابِيعَ مِنَ البَحْثِ. وَأَكْتُبُ عَمُودًا أُسْبُوعِيًّا.⁩
Laylā: I write inquiries: long topics that require weeks of research. And I keep a weekly column.
Luca: Have you ever had a scoop?

⁧مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً، قَبْلَ سَنَوَاتٍ. اليَوْمَ السَّبْقُ يَدُومُ دَقِيقَتَيْنِ:⁩ ( ⁧تَضْحَكُ⁩ ) ⁧لَيْلَى:⁩ ⁧تَنْشُرُهُ، وَبَعْدَ دَقِيقَتَيْنِ يَكُونُ فِي كُلِّ المَوَاقِعِ. لِذٰلِكَ نُفَضِّلُ أَنْ نَكُونَ⁩ ⁧الأَدَقَّ، لَا الأَسْرَعَ.⁩
Laylā: (laughs) Once, years ago. Today a scoop lasts two minutes: you publish it, and after two minutes it is on all sites. That's why we prefer to be the most precise, not the fastest.
Luca: And who funds the site?

⁧يَاسْمِين: هٰذَا هُوَ السُّؤَالُ! بَعْضُهَا صَحِيحٌ، وَبَعْضُهَا مُبَالَغٌ فِيهِ. وَالمُشْكِلَةُ أَنَّ الخَوَارِزْمِيَّةَ لَا تُكَافِئُ الدِّقَّةَ، بَلِ التَّفَاعُلَ: كُلَّمَا كَانَ المَقْطَعُ أَكْثَرَ إِثَارَةً، زَادَ انْتِشَارُهُ.⁩

Yāsmīn: That's the question! Some of them are true, some of them exaggerated. And the problem is that the algorithm doesn't reward accuracy, but interaction: the more sensational the video is, the more it spreads.
